items.title: 2.3 Experimental evidence for the electronic configuration

source_refs.note: Topic 2.3, printed page 25: the two sources of evidence introduced; the detail follows in 2.4.1 and 2.3.2 as printed.

blocks.text: The modern theory of electronic structure originates from the Bohr model of the atom. The evidence for this and the later models of the atom derives principally from two sources: atomic spectra and ionization energies. The next two topics take each in turn.

blocks.prompt: Why are two independent kinds of experiment needed to support a model of how electrons are arranged?
blocks.explanation: Atomic spectra show that electrons occupy fixed energy levels, because only certain wavelengths are emitted or absorbed. Ionization energies measure how tightly each electron is held and so reveal the shells. Each confirms the other, which is stronger evidence than either alone.

items: The theory of electronic structure grows from the Bohr model; its evidence comes from atomic spectra and ionization energies.
